newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Meurant quits to eliminate notion of bias.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Meurant quits to eliminate notion of bias.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Sept 30 - North Harbour rugby coach Brad Meurant says by standing down at the end of the season he hopes to eliminate the notion of bias when it comes to selecting his Super 12 side, the Waikato Chiefs.
Meurant said he had told the North Harbour Rugby Union at the time of his appointment that he only intended it to be for one season.
"It was never going to be for more than a season and I always told them that I would do it for a year and assess it after that," he told NZPA.
Meurant said the need to be seen as maintaining impartiality and the differing standards of professionalism at NPC level had eventually convinced him not to make himself available next year.
"It all came down to finding out what was happening with the Waikato Chiefs and whether you could do justice to two jobs.
"It is important that by doing this I have hopefully taken out the notion of bias when it comes to the Chiefs.

"Of course you're always thinking of the guys you've been involved with, but I think there might have been a few people who thought of the element of bias when the Chiefs lost their first three games this year.
"They probably thought I was being loyal to the Harbour players."
He said it was difficult to adjust to having an NPC team where some players were professional and others semi-professional or even amateur.
"At least with the Chiefs everyone is on a level playing field, even if they aren't being paid exactly the same," he said.
"But at Harbour a lot of players are semi-professional and are having to tie down other careers while playing in the NPC.
"I also felt holding down two different jobs made it difficult and perhaps compromised me a bit."
He said Harbour's poor NPC season did not have a lot to do with his decision to stand down.
"Not at all, of course we would have loved to have been in the final, it would have been a fairytale way to go out," he said.
"But that was not to be, we've had a disjointed season for various reasons, and it didn't have any bearing in my decision in the end."
He said by concentrating on being Chiefs' coach he could scout the region for talent a lot better, particularly while NPC games were going on.
"It makes it easier to get around and see who you've got and make your own decisions instead of having to rely on people," Meurant said.
"That's got to be a positive from the Chiefs' point of view."
And he'll be watching Friday night's Ranfurly Shield match between Auckland and Waikato with interest.
"It would be good for us to have a final crack at it, but you have to consider that it might be good for the rest of the country if the shield stays in Waikato."
North Harbour said goodbye to their Onewa Domain base on Saturday with a limp 27-15 win over King Country. They will play at their new Albany Stadium from next year.
